earlier_scan.source_named: Michael, Lev & Christine Beier 2012. Phonological sketch and classification of Aewa (ms., SSILA winter meeting); otherwise only wordlists (Tessmann 1930, Espinoza 1955, Villarejo 1959)

sources.citation: Beier, Christine & Lev Michael. 2019 draft (June 20, 2019) of: Beier & Michael 2023. Aʔɨwa. In P. Epps & L. Michael (eds.), Amazonian Languages: Language Isolates I, 173-222. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. DOI 10.1515/9783110419405-004. Sec. 2.1 on the names 'Aushiri/Abijira'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Its stress section (3.3) concerns Aʔɨwa (abis1238), not aush1242. For identity: 'León collected a brief wordlist.. reproduced by Granja (1942) (and again by Espinosa (1955: 67)).. Barrio.. under the name Ahuishiri-Shiripuno (Auka). Both León's and Barrio's lists reveal that the group or groups in question were speakers of Arabela (Zaparoan), as amply documented by Rich (1999)'; Ribeiro & Wise (1978) adopted 'Aushiri' for this Zaparoan group, which is the basis of Ethnologue's Aushiri [avs].

sources.citation: Michael, Lev. Curriculum vitae, 30 June 2019 (Internet Archive copy of linguistics.berkeley.edu/~levmichael/).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic check only: no Aushiri/Arabela-subgroup description listed; Zaparoan items are Iquito, Andoa, Záparo, and the Aʔɨwa handbook chapter.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Aushiri [avs] ('extinct dialect of Záparo.. Escuelacocha region'); the Aewa article's phonology tables concern abis1238.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record 'Aushiri' (aush1242) incl. classification comment (cites Michael, Beier & Wauters 2012) and Glottolog's most extensive description = 'wordlist or less' (Villarejo 1959; Espinosa Pérez 1955); plus Glottolog reference records 92457 (Espinosa Pérez 1955 'Indios avijiras', language code note: 'Ah-Shiripuno (Auka) C. Granja = Aushiri [avs], Ah-Vacacocha Tessmann = Tekiraka [ash]'), 139351 (Villarejo 1959), 145139 (Wise 2005).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; establishes that aush1242 is attested by word lists only (the Shiripuno 'Aushiri' lists reproduced in Espinosa 1955) and is distinct from Tekiraka/Aʔɨwa [ash].

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. Záparo stock, p. 160 ('Chiripuno - spoken on the Chiripunos River. [Granja 1942, pp. 114-138]') and comparative table 'ZÁPARO, STOCK II' (Chiripuno column: p-anák 'head', namixía 'eye', pananú 'sun', narexa 'star', ita 'house', muesaxi 'woman'); separately 'Auishiri, isolated language' [Tessmann 1930: 486].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
